title: RAS-GTP Inhibition Overcomes Acquired Resistance to KRASG12C Inhibitors Mediated by Oncogenic and Wild-Type RAS Activation in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
model: NCI-H358 parental (DMSO) and sotorasib-resistant H358-AMGR cells (on sotorasib), Addgene #75314 kinome library (3,149 guides, 763 genes, 100 non-targeting)
contrast: Sotorasib-resistant vs parental H358 after 2 weeks (2 vs 2 replicate cultures), library totals
paper_method: Not stated (heatmap of gene-aggregated test scores, Fig. 6F); no gene table published
paper_calls: Cell-cycle kinases PLK1, ATR, CHEK1, CDK1 and ILK, PTK2, ROCK2, FASTKD3, CDK15, RAB11FIP5 depleted in resistant cells; EGFR and MAPK1 more essential in parental cells
barcs_calls: 4 genes at FDR 0.10 after control calibration (MAPK1, EGFR, ROCK2, CDK15); 4 against the control null
named_hits: BARCS rank by p value (both directions): MAPK1 #1, EGFR #2, ROCK2 #3, CDK15 #4 (FDR < 0.10); FASTKD3 #5, RAB11FIP5 #6, PTK2 #7, ILK #10 (FDR 0.17-0.50); CDK1 #100, PLK1 #286, CHEK1 #639, ATR #708 (4/12 at FDR 0.10)
verdict: BARCS's top ten contains all eight kinases the paper calls differential between resistant and parental cells, with MAPK1, EGFR, ROCK2 and CDK15 at FDR 0.10, but the paper's headline cell-cycle kinases (PLK1, ATR, CHEK1, CDK1) drop out equally in both lines and are not resistance-specific dependencies.
